knowledge_base.interpretation: The KB was validated before and after this audit. Its very-high interface, public-information, CABT-semantics, version-binding, natural-seat, and no-manual-randomness rules remain binding. Route-specific rows are hypotheses until exact native transitions prove them.

authority_boundary.card_table_contains: numeric identity, type, HP, weakness/resistance, retreat, stage, attack IDs, damage and energy-count metadata
authority_boundary.card_table_does_not_bind: effect text execution, discard/recycle identity, damage modifiers, or per-effect timing
authority_boundary.policy_rule: No card-specific production authority may be derived from a PARTIAL route. A faithful reproduction of the old native anchor must be labeled FROZEN_CONTROL_REPRODUCTION and is not a new strategic result.

route_findings.label: Kyogre Riptide
source_facts: Official CSV and native API identify attack 1042, one Water energy cost, variable damage, and a recycle-like effect description.
Card table binds Kyogre 721 to attack 1042 with damage metadata 0 and one Water energy requirement.
live_evidence: All 14 had one public HP_CHANGE event.
Immediate actor deck-count deltas were 0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 11, 12, or 16, with no retained per-card transition proving the effect.
The report has zero recycle_basic_water_and_damage causal proofs.
cannot_assert: that damage is exactly 20 times the Basic Water count in the discard
that only Basic Water is recycled
that all eligible discard cards are recycled, or the exact timing of recycle versus damage
route_findings.upgrade_test: Run repeated native transitions with known public discard Basic Water counts and a legal Kyogre attack; retain before/after discard and deck counts, public movement events with card IDs where exposed, and HP delta. Require count identity and damage equation in more than one count stratum.

route_findings.label: Kyogre Swirling Waves
source_facts: Official CSV and native API identify a 130-damage attack with a two-Energy discard description.
Card table binds attack 1043 to 130 damage metadata and Water/Colorless/Colorless cost encoding.
live_evidence: One public HP_CHANGE event was observed.
The immediate deck delta was zero and the counted Energy-to-discard movement for Basic Water was zero.
The report has zero discard_two_energy_and_damage causal proofs.
cannot_assert: that two attached Energy cards are discarded
which Energy identities are selected when more than two are attached
whether the observed HP change is the full 130 after all modifiers
route_findings.upgrade_test: Use an actor Kyogre with at least three publicly identified attached Energy cards and a target with controlled HP/weakness/resistance; require exactly two attached-card movement events to discard and an independently reconciled damage delta.

route_findings.label: Surfing Beach
source_facts: Official CSV and native API identify Stadium 1262 with one Water-Pokemon switch skill.
Card table binds 1262 as a Stadium with one skill but contains no executable skill semantics.
live_evidence: Nine play/after observations and nine semantic requests were recorded.
The branch recorded zero skill actions and zero stadium_skill_water_switch causal proofs.
No executed, post-play switch event connects the Stadium to the requested skill in the retained aggregate.
cannot_assert: that it is once per player turn
that both Active and Bench targets must be Water Pokemon, or that non-Water choices are rejected
route_findings.upgrade_test: Play 1262, capture the subsequent SKILL request and execute it with visible Water Active/Bench cards; require a SWITCH event with the same actor and serials, then attempt a second skill in the same turn and a non-Water target in a separate fixture.

route_findings.label: Mega Abomasnow Hammer-lanche
source_facts: Official CSV and native API identify a six-card top-deck discard and variable 100-damage-per-Basic-Water description.
Card table binds attack 1046 to damage metadata 0 and two Water energy requirements.
live_evidence: Every observed attack had actor deck-count delta -6 and one HP_CHANGE event.
Observed HP_CHANGE values were -100, -300, -400, -500, and -600 with counts 1, 3, 11, 6, and 1 respectively.
The report has zero discard_top_six_and_damage causal proofs, so the six cards and their Basic-Water identities are not causally retained as a complete transition.
cannot_assert: that exactly the top six cards were moved to discard rather than another engine transition producing the same count delta
that each 100-damage increment corresponds exactly to a Basic Water card among those six
that the damage values are unmodified base values in all contexts
route_findings.upgrade_test: Retain all six native public movement events and card identities for several attacks, reconcile deck -6 and discard +6, count Basic Water among exactly those six, and reconcile HP delta after weakness/resistance. Repeat across zero, one, and multiple Basic-Water top-six strata.

route_findings.label: Mega Abomasnow Frost Barrier
source_facts: Official CSV and native API identify a 200-damage attack and a next-opponent-turn damage reduction description.
Card table binds attack 1047 to damage metadata 200 and three Water energy requirements.
live_evidence: Four attack selections were observed and each had one HP_CHANGE event.
The retained branch recorded four post_barrier_hp_events:0 observations.
The report deliberately does not infer a damage modifier from those trajectories and has no causal proof.
cannot_assert: that it applies only during the opponent's next turn
whether weakness/resistance ordering, damage counters, effects, or repeated attacks interact with the modifier
route_findings.upgrade_test: Run paired native fixtures with identical public setup, a known opponent attack and no weakness/resistance confound; compare next-turn HP delta after Frost Barrier versus a no-Barrier control, then test a later turn and a damage-counter effect separately.

upgrade_decision.reason: The source CSV/native API text is metadata and the Phase A aggregate contains observations but not sufficient per-card causal transition proofs. The strict status matrix remains authoritative.
upgrade_decision.safe_control_translation: A standalone policy may reproduce the frozen native anchor's observed priorities for a control comparison, but it must not present those partial-effect assumptions as newly validated strategic rules.

P0_hidden_boundary.risk: A public-only typed policy can still accidentally use raw/private data, hidden entity identities, selection-local identifiers, or opponent hand identities if the adapter leaks them.
required_tests: Static import/source scan rejects NativeRulePolicy, private baseline paths, native raw mappings, cg imports, and opponent-hand traversal from the candidate policy module.
Adversarial observations vary hidden opponent hand/deck/Prize identities while preserving public counts and legal options; action semantic choice must be unchanged.
Opponent hand must be None in the semantic snapshot; visible revealed cards and hand_count remain legal public inputs.
Selection-local deck/looking cards are allowed only because the engine exposes them to the acting player; they must not be treated as a durable deck-order oracle.

P0_option_contract.risk: Scoring raw indexes, a fixed prefix, or a stale request can silently miss legal lines or submit invalid references.
required_tests: Every option is scored and the final adapter validates type, bounds, availability, uniqueness, source/target semantics, and request identity.
Permute every option list and require the same semantic choice; compare set equivalence for UNORDERED and sequence equivalence for ORDERED requests.

Tie fixtures include duplicate semantic fingerprints and distinct cards with the same card ID; the tie policy must be deterministic without consulting original_index or input order, or fail closed on ambiguous ties.
A forged option with changed source/target/card role but reused original_index or fingerprint is rejected.

P0_perspective.risk: A policy or outcome aggregator hard-coded to player 0 can invert target/attacker logic and report the wrong WDL.
required_tests: Run the same semantic board with acting_player 0 and 1 and verify self/opponent roles follow acting_player.
Mirror a two-player synthetic fixture and require corresponding action semantics, not fixed player IDs.
Aggregate candidate score as winner==candidate_player, draw==0.5, loss==0; retain actual first_player separately.

P0_compound_action.risk: A deterministic scorer can produce a valid-looking prefix but fail ordered multi-select, optional selection, or STOP legality.
required_tests: Cover min=max=0, mandatory single, optional 0..1, mandatory multi-select, optional multi-select with early STOP, and max-count completion.
STOP is emitted only after min_count and before max_count; it is never emitted at max_count or before minimum.
Ordered SKILL_ORDER preserves semantic sequence; UNORDERED equivalence compares sets while still submitting unique original indexes.
Validate the full retained decoder trace and semantic fingerprints, not only submitted indexes.

P0_lifecycle.risk: State can leak across games, players, policies, workers, or stale requests even if individual actions are legal.
required_tests: Reset on start/deck, terminal, error, and worker replacement; assert no active state survives the relevant boundary.
Use two episode UUIDs and both player indexes with the same policy class; assert independent ledgers and no cross-player memory.
Duplicate identical (selection_seq, request_id) is idempotent; a reused request_id with changed request content is rejected rather than returning a cached action.
Stale and out-of-order selection sequences fail closed.

P1_provenance_and_harness.risk: A passing local tournament can be unreviewable if candidate perspective, source scope, hashes, dirty state, or immutable evidence are ambiguous.
required_tests: Manifest actual engine library, game/API/sim wrappers, card CSV, card-table semantic hash, exact candidate and opponent deck hashes, candidate source/config hashes, resolved config, command, platform, Git commit and dirty digest.
Use a candidate-only source hash; the existing broad source_tree_hash includes all source/config dirty work and does not by itself identify the candidate implementation.
Seal completed run artifacts read-only or content-address them; a sidecar digest alone does not make writable JSON immutable.
Resume validates every existing match record against its digest and immutable run plan; never trust arbitrary files in matches/.
Retain per-worker terminal/failure/fallback/timeout/invalid counters, action latency, CPU/RSS, and missing-output worker failures.

P1_private_baseline_coupling.risk: The existing arena's rule adapter is intentionally private-baseline-backed; reusing that path for the new candidate would contaminate the standalone policy claim.
required_tests: Candidate module imports only public G1 models/actions/environment and deterministic public-state/profile modules plus numeric card-table metadata.
Static and runtime checks prove no private baseline module is loaded by the candidate path.
Private native anchors remain opponent/control specs only; their decks and receipt hashes are manifest inputs, not candidate implementation dependencies.

existing_harness_red_flags.finding: The existing aggregator computes player0_score_mean, not candidate-perspective WDL. Reusing it for a candidate-versus-anchor claim can invert all games where the candidate is policy1.

The built-in policy registry only exposes random, first, and private rule adapters. A standalone candidate must use a separate public policy registration path and must not be implemented as NativeRulePolicy.
The broad source hash and Git dirty digest are useful run context but do not provide a candidate-only source/config hash; unrelated dirty work is intentionally present.
write_immutable_json uses exclusive creation and fsync but does not seal files read-only. A digest sidecar is integrity evidence, not immutable storage by itself.
Resume trusts existing match JSON files by game_id and does not independently verify per-record content hashes against an append-only manifest.

next_falsifiable_work_order: Keep all five route statuses PARTIAL and exclude their effect-specific rules from production authority.
Finish public-only standalone control and contract tests first: permutation, semantic tie behavior, perspective, STOP/multiselect, lifecycle, and private-baseline scan.
Repair candidate-perspective and provenance/immutability requirements in the Phase B harness before any policy-strength tournament.

Build one exact native causal fixture at a time, starting with Swirling Waves or Surfing Beach because their expected transitions are easiest to isolate; re-query the KB after every surprising result.
Run only the one-request-per-cell mechanical canary until the independent contract review passes; do not launch Kaggle or claim route improvement from this audit.
